Committee: Ways and Means Education
Sponsor: Pringle
Analyst: Jessica Perez
Date: 03/01/2021
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 126 as introduced repeals various tax exemptions for entities that do not have a current certificate of exemption, according to the Department of Revenue. In addition, this bill extends the current tax exemption for certain entities to include collecting certain taxes, which could decrease receipts to the Education Trust Fund, the State General Fund, counties, and municipalities by an undetermined amount dependent upon the amount of taxes previous collected by each entity that will no longer be collected.
Bill Poole, Chair
Ways and Means Education

Committee: Ways and Means Education
Sponsor: Pringle
Analyst: Jessica Perez
Date: 03/10/2021
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 126 as substituted and reported by the Committee on Ways and Means Education provides that certain entities that are statutorily exempt from payment or collection of various taxes, but who have not obtained a certificate of exemption as provided by current law since January 1, 2016, shall no longer be entitled to the exemption, beginning January 1, 2022. This bill further provides that, beginning January 1, 2023 and annually thereafter, any such statutorily-exempt entity that has not renewed its certificate of exemption during the previous five years shall no longer be entitled to the exemption. This bill will not directly affect state or local funding.
Bill Poole, Chair
Ways and Means Education
